### Observed differences

- Resource allocation turned over across much of the process. In the earlier window, activities A01, A03, A13, A14, A17 and A21 were each handled by a stable mix of resources in which a consistent group led — for example User_49 took roughly 7–12 in every 100 assignments of each of these activities. In the later window, most of that leading group no longer appears among the top shares and a largely different group took over — for example User_56 now handles about 6–11 in 100 — while only a few resources continued in both windows; the unnamed long tail also grew (for A01, from about 38 to 45 in 100 assignments). [ASSIGN001, ASSIGN002, ASSIGN004, ASSIGN005, ASSIGN006, ASSIGN007]
- A08 changed most sharply: in the earlier window its work was spread over 17 distinct resources with the largest holding about 18 in 100 assignments; in the later window every assignment goes to the single resource User_121 (concentration index from about 0.11 to 1.0), based on 108 versus 120 traces. [ASSIGN003, CONC001]
- In the later window, the elapsed time from the completion of A04 to that of A01 lengthened in its upper tail: the median gap stayed near 24–25 hours in both windows, but the mean rose from about 26.5 to 44 hours and the 75th percentile from about 31 to 71 hours (200 gap measurements per window; the difference exceeds about 999.5 of 1,000 random re-splits). [TWAIT001]
- A rare, near-instantaneous A20-to-A10 handover appears in more traces in the later window (about 8–9 in 100 versus about 3–4 in 100), but the gap itself is a fraction of a second in both windows, so this difference is practically negligible. [TWAIT002]
- The only qualifying differences are the timing and resource items above; no control-flow unit passed screening (0 items against roughly 0.16 expected when nothing has changed), so no structural or routing difference is indicated. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002, ASSIGN001, ASSIGN002, ASSIGN003, ASSIGN004, ASSIGN005, ASSIGN006, ASSIGN007, CONC001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that resource allocation changed. In the later window, A08 is assigned entirely to one resource (User_121) where it was previously spread across about 17 resources, and across A01, A03, A13, A14, A17 and A21 the workload moved from one group of recurring resources to a largely different group, with a few resources continuing in both windows. This rests on direct allocation measurements: the resource family produced 8 qualifying items against roughly 0.005 expected without change, the same resources gain and lose across activities, and each profile is backed by roughly 108–274 traces per window. Limitations: A13 and A14 (and A01 and A03) show nearly identical profiles, so their items are not independent confirmations; the identifiers are anonymous codes, so no roles can be inferred; and the evidence cannot distinguish a change in assignment rules from a different pool of resources simply being available in the later window. [ASSIGN001, ASSIGN002, ASSIGN003, ASSIGN004, ASSIGN005, ASSIGN006, ASSIGN007, CONC001]

Other differences: a timing change stands on its own — the A04-to-A01 completion gap's slow tail grew (mean up about 17.5 hours, 75th percentile up about 40 hours, median stable), and with 2 time items against roughly 0.02 expected without change it would qualify as a timing hypothesis in its own right; the evidence cannot show whether it is connected to the allocation change. The A20-to-A10 item is statistically unusual but practically negligible. No control-flow difference qualified, so no reordering or path change is indicated. [TWAIT001, TWAIT002]
